backlog.title: Stream Integrity & Shortcut Lifecycle Bugfix
backlog.description: Fix the three defects found by validating the extension's output stream against the real pi-agent-core consumer: (1) CRITICAL — reasoning content lost from the persisted assistant message on every interruption (contentIndex collision + partial switching); (2) MAJOR — shortcut remains armed during answer generation, aborting the in-progress answer; (3) MINOR — single coordinator active-proxy slot loses shortcut coverage for overlapping streams. All three are internal changes to src/provider/proxy.ts and src/state/coordinator.ts. No new public API, config flag, or CLI surface. The existing 380-test suite has a blind spot (asserts on raw forwarded events, never runs the real consumer assembly), so a consumer-simulation harness is built first as foundational test infra.

milestones.title: Consumer-Simulation Harness & Realistic Mocks
milestones.description: Build the test infrastructure that the existing suite lacks: a faithful copy of the pi-agent-core agent-loop consumer assembly logic (partialMessage = event.partial; finalMessage = stream.result()), plus a realistic two-call mock provider that carries real accumulating partial objects and contentIndex fields (mirroring the real openai-completions provider). This harness is what would have caught Issue 1. It is consumed by the Issue 1 integration test (M2) and is reusable for Issue 2 (M3) lifecycle assertions. Pure test infra — NO production source changes.

tasks.title: Build consumer-simulation harness and realistic two-call mock provider
tasks.description: Create tests/helpers/consumer-harness.ts containing (a) a consumeLikeAgentLoop function that faithfully mirrors agent-loop.js message assembly, and (b) a realistic two-call mock provider whose primary and replacement calls each build a real accumulating output object with structured content blocks and proper contentIndex (exactly like openai-completions.js does). This is the foundational tooling for reproducing and verifying Issue 1.

subtasks.title: Create consumeLikeAgentLoop consumer-simulation harness
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_b0c6691bb424/bugfix/001_05591a24a0d0/architecture/pi-agent-core-consumer.md §1 for the EXACT agent-loop.js consumer logic (lines ~194-249). The consumer does `partialMessage = event.partial` on EVERY non-terminal event, then `finalMessage = await stream.result()` (which resolves to the done event's message field). This is the assembly path that the existing tests never exercise.
2. INPUT: An AssistantMessageEventStream (the proxy's output stream) — the same interface Pi's agent-loop iterates.
3. LOGIC: Create `tests/helpers/consumer-harness.ts` exporting `async function consumeLikeAgentLoop(stream: AssistantMessageEventStream): Promise<{ finalMessage: AssistantMessage; events: AssistantMessageEvent[]; partialHistory: AssistantMessage[] }>`. The function iterates the stream with `for await (const event of stream)`, records each event in `events`, and on every event that carries `event.partial` records a shallow copy into `partialHistory` (mirroring `partialMessage = event.partial`). After the loop, resolve `finalMessage = await stream.result()` (with a timeout race to fail fast). Return all three. This mirrors agent-loop.js EXACTLY — do NOT add contentIndex-indexing logic here (that is the proxy.js path; the agent-loop path relies entirely on event.partial following). Add a small unit test in the same file or a companion test that feeds a hand-built event stream (start+thinking+text+done with realistic partials) through the harness and asserts finalMessage.content has both blocks — proving the harness assembles correctly.
4. OUTPUT: The exported `consumeLikeAgentLoop` function, consumed by P1.M2.T3.S1 (the Issue 1 integration test) and reusable by P1.M3.T2.S1. No production code touched.
5. MOCKING: None — this IS the test double. It consumes any AssistantMessageEventStream.
6. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change (test infrastructure only).

subtasks.title: Create realistic two-call mock provider with accumulating partial objects and contentIndex
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_b0c6691bb424/bugfix/001_05591a24a0d0/architecture/pi-ai-event-types.md §2-3 and pi-agent-core-consumer.md §3. The real openai-completions provider (node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js) builds ONE accumulating `output` object per call: `{ role:'assistant', content:[], ... }`, pushes content blocks into `output.content`, derives `contentIndex = blocks.indexOf(block)`, and stamps EVERY event with `partial: output` (the live reference). With reasoning ON (primary), a thinking block lands at content[0]; with reasoning OFF (replacement), the text block lands at content[0]. Both use contentIndex 0 — the collision. The terminal done carries `message: output`.
2. INPUT: None (this is a test-factory).
3. LOGIC: Create `tests/helpers/realistic-mock.ts` exporting `function makeRealisticTwoPhaseMock(opts?)` that returns `{ fn, calls, pushPrimary, pushReplacement, closePrimary, primaryOutput, replacementOutput }`. CRITICAL: unlike the existing placeholder mocks (which emit `ev({type:'text_start', contentIndex:0})` with NO partial), THIS mock must build a REAL accumulating `output` per call (exactly like the provider): `const output = { role:'assistant', content:[], model:'glm-4.7', usage:{...}, stopReason:'stop', timestamp:Date.now() }`. The 1st call (primary, reasoning:'high') pushes a `{type:'thinking', thinking:''}` block to output.content[0] and emits `start` (partial:output), `thinking_start` (contentIndex:0, partial:output), `thinking_delta` (contentIndex:0, delta, partial:output — appending to the block.thinking), `thinking_end`. The 2nd call (replacement, reasoning:undefined) builds a FRESH `output` (content:[]), pushes `{type:'text', text:''}` to its content[0], and emits `start`(suppressed by proxy), `text_start`(contentIndex:0, partial:freshOutput), `text_delta`(contentIndex:0), `done`(message:freshOutput). Expose `primaryOutput`/`replacementOutput` for assertions. The mock must throw on its AbortSignal abort (mirroring provider behavior), exactly like the existing makeScriptedTwoPhaseUpstream in tests/helpers/invariant-harness.ts. Record `calls` with the replacement's options (to assert reasoning===undefined).
4. OUTPUT: The mock factory, consumed by P1.M2.T1.S1 (capture test), P1.M2.T3.S1 (integration test). The accumulating `output` references let tests assert exact content-block structure.
5. MOCKING: This IS the mock. It simulates the real provider's output-accumulation behavior.
6. DOCS: none — test infrastructure only.

milestones.title: Issue 1 — Reasoning Content Preservation (Critical)
milestones.description: Fix the CRITICAL defect: on every interruption the reasoning content is silently dropped from the persisted assistant message. The StreamProxy forwards replacement events verbatim, causing (a) a contentIndex collision (primary thinking at [0], replacement text at [0]) and (b) partial switching (the replacement's fresh text-only partial replaces the accumulated reasoning in the agent-loop consumer). The fix: the proxy captures the primary's frozen content blocks at the abort boundary, then REWRITES replacement events — offsetting contentIndex past the primary's blocks and merging each event's partial (and the done message) into a single unified [thinking, text] message. This is the core use-case bug (100% of interruptions).

tasks.title: Capture primary frozen content blocks at the abort boundary
tasks.description: Add data-plumbing to StreamProxy so the primary stream's structured content blocks (the thinking blocks from event.partial) are captured and deep-cloned at the freeze boundary. This produces the frozen block array and the contentIndex offset that the replacement-event rewrite (T2) consumes.

subtasks.title: Capture primary partial content blocks and compute contentIndex offset at freeze
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_b0c6691bb424/bugfix/001_05591a24a0d0/architecture/system_context.md §Issue 1 + pi-ai-event-types.md §2. The primary stream's events each carry `event.partial` = the provider's live accumulating `output` object (same reference, content blocks at output.content). The proxy currently ignores these partials. We need the structured content blocks (e.g. `{type:'thinking', thinking:'...'}`) — NOT just the raw delta strings in ReasoningBuffer (which lack block structure). The freeze happens in run()'s catch/abort branch right after `this._buffer.freeze()`.
2. INPUT: Primary events flowing through run()'s loop (each has `event.partial: AssistantMessage`). The realistic mock from P1.M1.T1.S2 provides events with real accumulating partials.
3. LOGIC: In src/provider/proxy.ts: (a) Add private fields `private _primaryPartial: AssistantMessage | undefined` and `private _frozenPrimaryContent: ReadonlyArray<Record<string, unknown>> = []` and `private _contentIndexOffset = 0`. (b) In run()'s primary `for await` loop, right after `this.trackEvent(event); this._emit(event);`, add: `if (event.partial) this._primaryPartial = event.partial;` (capture the live reference on every primary event — the last one wins, which has the most-complete content). (c) In the abort branch of run()'s catch (the block that calls `this._buffer.freeze()`), AFTER freeze(), deep-clone the content blocks: `this._frozenPrimaryContent = (this._primaryPartial?.content ?? []).map(b => ({ ...b }));` and `this._contentIndexOffset = this._frozenPrimaryContent.length;`. Use a shallow-per-block clone (`{...b}`) — blocks are plain data objects; this captures the frozen state before any post-abort mutation. GUARD: if `_primaryPartial` is undefined (placeholder mocks with no partial), frozen content is `[]` and offset is 0 — the rewrite (T2) becomes a no-op, preserving existing test behavior.
4. OUTPUT: `this._frozenPrimaryContent` (the frozen thinking blocks) and `this._contentIndexOffset` (the count) are populated and available for P1.M2.T2.S1. Write a test (using the realistic mock) that drives a primary stream, triggers abort mid-reasoning, and asserts `_frozenPrimaryContent` has one `{type:'thinking'}` block with the accumulated thinking text and `_contentIndexOffset === 1`.
5. MOCKING: Use the realistic two-call mock from P1.M1.T1.S2. Mock the diagnostics with the capturing stub pattern from tests/helpers/invariant-harness.ts.
6. DOCS: none — internal data plumbing, no user-facing surface change.

tasks.title: Rewrite replacement events to merge primary reasoning with answer content
tasks.description: In StreamProxy._emit() (the single forwarding chokepoint), when authority is 'splicing' and frozen primary content was captured, transform every replacement event before pushing: offset its contentIndex past the primary's blocks, and rewrite its partial (and the terminal done/error message) to a merged AssistantMessage whose content is [...frozenPrimaryBlocks, ...replacementBlocks]. This makes the consumer assemble a single unified [thinking, text] message.

subtasks.title: Rewrite non-terminal replacement events: contentIndex offset + partial merge
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_b0c6691bb424/bugfix/001_05591a24a0d0/architecture/system_context.md §Issue 1 + pi-agent-core-consumer.md §1-2. The _emit() method in src/provider/proxy.ts is the SINGLE chokepoint: both primary and replacement events pass through it. In the splicing branch (`this._authority === 'splicing'`), replacement events are currently pushed verbatim via `this._output.push(event)`. The local consumer does `partialMessage = event.partial` on every event; the remote consumer indexes `partial.content[contentIndex]`. BOTH must be fixed: offset contentIndex so the answer lands after the thinking blocks, AND merge the partial so the streaming view and result() retain the thinking.
2. INPUT: `this._frozenPrimaryContent` and `this._contentIndexOffset` from P1.M2.T1.S1. Replacement events arriving in _emit()'s splicing branch (each has `event.contentIndex` and `event.partial`).
3. LOGIC: In src/provider/proxy.ts _emit(), in the splicing branch, BEFORE the final `this._output.push(event)`, add a rewrite gate: `if (this._contentIndexOffset > 0 && 'contentIndex' in event) { event = this._rewriteReplacementEvent(event); }`. Implement `private _rewriteReplacementEvent(event)` returning a new event object: `{ ...event, contentIndex: event.contentIndex + this._contentIndexOffset, partial: this._mergePartial(event.partial) }`. Implement `private _mergePartial(replacementPartial)` returning `{ ...replacementPartial, content: [...this._frozenPrimaryContent.map(b=>({...b})), ...(replacementPartial?.content ?? [])] }` — prepend CLONED frozen blocks (clone each to avoid shared mutable references) then the replacement's own content. The `if (this._contentIndexOffset > 0)` guard is CRITICAL: when offset is 0 (no captured primary content — e.g. existing placeholder-mock tests), the rewrite is a no-op so the existing 380 tests stay green. Handle EC-017 (replacement returned reasoning): the replacement's own thinking blocks are in its partial.content and get prepended-after-frozen automatically — correct, no special case needed. Also apply the rewrite to the suppressed/discard guards BEFORE they early-return (a thinking event from the replacement that is forwarded must be rewritten too). Write a test: drive the realistic mock, triggerStop, collect forwarded replacement events, assert each non-terminal replacement event has `contentIndex === 1` (offset) and `event.partial.content` has BOTH a thinking block (index 0) and the growing text block (index 1).
4. OUTPUT: Forwarded non-terminal replacement events carry offset contentIndex and merged partials. Consumed by P1.M2.T2.S2 (terminal rewrite) and P1.M2.T3.S1 (integration test).
5. MOCKING: Realistic two-call mock from P1.M1.T1.S2. Capturing diagnostics stub.
6. DOCS: none — internal event transformation, no user-facing surface change.

subtasks.title: Rewrite replacement terminal event: merge done message (and error) content
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_b0c6691bb424/bugfix/001_05591a24a0d0/architecture/pi-ai-event-types.md §3 + pi-agent-core-consumer.md §1. The consumer resolves the PERSISTED message via `finalMessage = await stream.result()`, which resolves to the `done` event's `message` field. The replacement's `done` carries `message: output_repl` (text-only). If forwarded verbatim, result() resolves to text-only — reasoning lost from history. push(done) IMMEDIATELY resolves result() with event.message, so the merge MUST happen BEFORE the push. The error terminal similarly carries `error: output_repl`.
2. INPUT: `this._frozenPrimaryContent` + `this._contentIndexOffset` from P1.M2.T1.S1. The replacement's done/error events in _emit()'s splicing branch.
3. LOGIC: In src/provider/proxy.ts _rewriteReplacementEvent (or the splicing terminal path), handle terminal events: for `done` → `{ ...event, message: this._mergePartial(event.message) }` (merge frozen blocks into the done message's content); for `error` → `{ ...event, error: this._mergePartial(event.error) }`. The _mergePartial from P1.M2.T2.S1 prepends frozen primary blocks. GUARD: same `this._contentIndexOffset > 0` condition — no-op when offset is 0 (preserves existing error-path tests). NOTE: terminal events do NOT have a contentIndex field, so they skip the contentIndex-offset part but still need the message/error content merge. Ensure the gate in _emit applies the merge to terminals: the `if (this._contentIndexOffset > 0)` check covers both (terminals have no contentIndex but the merge is on message/error). Write a test: drive realistic mock, triggerStop, consume via consumeLikeAgentLoop, assert `finalMessage.content` block types === ['thinking','text'] and the thinking block text matches the primary reasoning.
4. OUTPUT: The done event's message (and error's error) carry merged [thinking, text] content. Consumed by P1.M2.T3.S1 (full integration test).
5. MOCKING: Realistic two-call mock from P1.M1.T1.S2 + consumeLikeAgentLoop from P1.M1.T1.S1.
6. DOCS: none — internal terminal transformation.

milestones.title: Issue 2 — Shortcut Disablement After Reasoning Ends (Major)
milestones.description: Fix the MAJOR defect: the FSM has no normal exit from Reasoning, so the controller stays in Reasoning for the entire answer phase, keeping canInterrupt() true. Pressing the shortcut during answer generation aborts the in-progress answer and launches a fresh replacement. The fix uses a minimal reasoningEnded flag (set on thinking_end / first answer token per PRD §22.4) to gate canInterrupt() and triggerStop(), disabling the shortcut the moment reasoning ends. This also prevents compounding Issue 1 (re-aborting the answer).

tasks.title: Add reasoningEnded flag and gate shortcut availability
tasks.description: Add a private _reasoningEnded flag to StreamProxy, set it in trackEvent() on the PRD §22.4 leave-conditions (thinking_end, text_start, toolcall_start while in Reasoning), and gate both canInterrupt() and triggerStop()'s entry guard on it. The FSM (controller.ts) is NOT modified — the flag approach avoids breaking the §16 table and existing tests that assert the controller stays in Reasoning on normal completion.

subtasks.title: Add _reasoningEnded flag, set on §22.4 leave-conditions, gate canInterrupt() and triggerStop()
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_b0c6691bb424/bugfix/001_05591a24a0d0/architecture/system_context.md §Issue 2. Root cause: ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS (src/state/controller.ts) has no normal Reasoning→* exit; trackEvent() in src/provider/proxy.ts does nothing on thinking_end/text_start/toolcall_start; controller stays in Reasoning; canInterrupt() returns state==='Reasoning' → true during the answer. The fix is the minimal flag approach (NOT the FSM-extension approach) to avoid breaking stream-proxy-lifecycle.test.ts line ~441 which asserts getState()==='Reasoning' on normal completion. trackEvent() runs ONLY in the primary loop (replacement events do NOT run trackEvent — the buffer is frozen), so the flag correctly applies only to the primary reasoning phase.
2. INPUT: trackEvent(event) in src/provider/proxy.ts — the per-event reasoning-detection side effect that runs before _emit in run()'s primary loop. The event union and type guards from src/types.ts.
3. LOGIC: In src/provider/proxy.ts: (a) Add `private _reasoningEnded = false;`. (b) In trackEvent(), add a new detection step AFTER step 3 (the thinking_delta accumulation) and BEFORE the terminal handling: `if (this._controller.getState() === 'Reasoning' && (event.type === 'thinking_end' || isTextEvent(event) || isToolCallEvent(event))) { this._reasoningEnded = true; }`. This covers all three §22.4 leave-conditions (thinking_end OR first answer token). Setting a boolean multiple times is harmless (idempotent). (c) Change canInterrupt() from `return this._controller.canInterrupt();` to `return this._controller.getState() === 'Reasoning' && !this._reasoningEnded;`. (d) In triggerStop(), change the guard from `if (!this._controller.canInterrupt()) return false;` to `if (!this.canInterrupt()) return false;` so the proxy-level flag gate is enforced at the abort entry point (not just the controller's state check). (e) Update the JSDoc on canInterrupt() and trackEvent() to document the new flag + §22.4 leave-conditions. Write a unit test: drive start→thinking_start→thinking_delta→thinking_end, assert proxy.canInterrupt()===false and proxy.triggerStop()===false and no abort/replacement; repeat with thinking_delta→text_start (EC-006: first answer token) asserting the same.
4. OUTPUT: canInterrupt() returns false once reasoning ends; triggerStop() is a no-op. Consumed by P1.M3.T2.S1 (end-to-end tests). The controller FSM is UNCHANGED.
5. MOCKING: Use the existing mock patterns from tests/stream-proxy-abort.test.ts (scripted events). The realistic mock is optional here (this fix is about FSM/gating, not partials).
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on StreamProxy.canInterrupt() and StreamProxy.trackEvent() in src/provider/proxy.ts to document the reasoningEnded flag and the PRD §22.4 leave-conditions. This rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: Issue 3 — Coordinator Overlap Guard (Minor)
milestones.description: Fix the MINOR defect: StreamProxy._terminate() unconditionally clears the coordinator's active proxy, so if two eligible streams overlap and the non-active one terminates, it disables the shortcut for the still-active stream. The fix adds a guarded clearActiveProxy(proxy) method to TransitionCoordinator that only clears when the terminating proxy IS the currently-active one.

subtasks.title: Add clearActiveProxy(proxy) guard to coordinator, wire into _terminate, add overlap test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_b0c6691bb424/bugfix/001_05591a24a0d0/architecture/system_context.md §Issue 3. Root cause: src/provider/proxy.ts _terminate() calls `this._coordinator?.setActiveProxy(undefined)` UNCONDITIONALLY (line in the resource-release section). src/state/coordinator.ts holds a single `private activeProxy: ActiveProxy | undefined`. If proxy B overwrites A as active (setActiveProxy(B)), then A._terminate() clears the coordinator (undefined) even though B is still reasoning — B loses coverage. The fix: only clear if the terminating proxy IS the active one. StreamProxy is structurally assignable to ActiveProxy (it has isReasoning/canInterrupt/triggerStop/isInterrupting/isDelegating), so passing `this` type-checks.
2. INPUT: TransitionCoordinator (src/state/coordinator.ts) — the session-scoped coordinator with `private activeProxy` and `setActiveProxy`. StreamProxy._terminate() (src/provider/proxy.ts) — the single cleanup handler.
3. LOGIC: In src/state/coordinator.ts: add a public method `clearActiveProxy(proxy: ActiveProxy): void { if (this.activeProxy === proxy) { this.activeProxy = undefined; this.pendingStop = false; this.diagnostics.trace('coordinator.clear-active', {}); } }`. (Do NOT expose the private activeProxy field — the guard is encapsulated in the method. If a getter is needed for tests, add `get activeProxy()` returning `this.activeProxy` OR test via requestStop() behavior.) In src/provider/proxy.ts _terminate(): replace `this._coordinator?.setActiveProxy(undefined);` with `this._coordinator?.clearActiveProxy(this);`. Update _terminate()'s JSDoc to note the conditional clear. Write a test in tests/transition-coordinator.test.ts: create a coordinator + two mock ActiveProxy objects (or two real proxies via buildProxy); setActiveProxy(A); setActiveProxy(B) (B overwrites); call coordinator.clearActiveProxy(A) → assert activeProxy is still B (A was not active); call clearActiveProxy(B) → assert activeProxy is undefined (B was active). Also verify clearActiveProxy resets pendingStop only when it actually clears.
4. OUTPUT: Overlapping streams no longer lose shortcut coverage. Consumed by the full suite (all _terminate paths now use the guarded clear).
5. MOCKING: Mock ActiveProxy objects (plain objects with the 5 methods) or real StreamProxy instances via buildProxy from invariant-harness.ts.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on TransitionCoordinator.clearActiveProxy (new method) and StreamProxy._terminate() in src/provider/proxy.ts to document the conditional-clear behavior. This rides WITH the work.
